headline: LPG price rises by Tk 70 for August
summary: The price of a 12kg LPG cylinder has increased to Tk 1,598, effective from Sunday evening.
details: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the price of private sector liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for August. The price of the most commonly used 12kg LPG cylinder has risen by Tk 70, bringing the new price to Tk 1,598 from Tk 1,528.
The new pricing is effective from 6 PM on Sunday. BERC stated that the price per kg of LPG has increased by Tk 5.85, making the new rate Tk 133.15 per kg, up from the previous rate of Tk 127.30.
The price hike comes amid a pipeline gas supply crisis in the country. Many households have shifted to LPG cylinders for cooking due to the shortage of piped gas.

The increase is attributed to rising LPG prices in the global market following the conflict in the Middle East. This follows a previous sharp increase in April, where the price of a 12kg cylinder rose by Tk 387 and then by Tk 200 in the same month.

While private LPG prices rose, the price of a 12.5kg cylinder supplied by government companies remains unchanged at Tk 825. Additionally, auto gas prices have been reduced to Tk 70.40 per liter from Tk 86.93.

BERC determines the LPG price monthly based on theSaudi Aramco Contract Price (CP), based on which the domestic price is adjusted. The commission also considers the average dollar exchange rate from importer invoices.
caption:
LPG prices are up again. A 12kg cylinder now costs Tk 1,598.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the price of private sector liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for August. The price of the most commonly used 12kg LPG cylinder has risen by Tk 70, bringing the new price to Tk 1,598 from Tk 1,528.

The new pricing is effective from 6 PM on Sunday. BERC stated that the price per kg of LPG has increased by Tk 5.85, making the new rate Tk 133.15 per kg, up from the previous rate of Tk 127.30.

The price hike comes amid a pipeline gas supply crisis in the country. Many households have shifted to LPG cylinders for cooking due to the shortage of piped gas.

The increase is attributed to rising LPG prices in the global market following the conflict in the Middle East. This follows a previous sharp increase in April, where the price of a 12kg cylinder rose by Tk 387 and then by Tk 200 in the same month.

While private LPG prices rose, the price of a 12.5kg cylinder supplied by government companies remains unchanged at Tk 825. Additionally, auto gas prices have been reduced to Tk 70.40 per liter from Tk 86.93.

BERC determines the LPG price monthly based on theSaudi Aramco Contract Price (CP), based on which the domestic price is adjusted. The commission also considers the average dollar exchange rate from importer invoices.

headline: UAE court grants bail to ex-IGP Benazir Ahmed but bars him from leaving
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed confirms the bail but reveals the government has hired a law firm in the UAE to seek its cancellation.
details: Former inspector general of police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed has been granted bail by a UAE court on the condition that he remains within the country, according to Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.
The Home Minister stated that while bail was granted, the full terms of the order are not yet known. He has requested certified copies of the order to understand the specific conditions.
In response to the gelişme, the Bangladesh government has appointed a law firm in the UAE to pursue the cancellation of Benazir Ahmed's bail.
Benazir Ahmed was arrested in Dubai in June following an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of the Bangladesh government.
The process to repatriate the former IGP to Bangladesh for trial is ongoing as the government continues its legal battle in the UAE.
caption:
Ex-IGP Benazir Ahmed granted bail in UAE, but he's barred from leaving the country. The Bangladesh government is now fighting to cancel it.

Former inspector general of police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed has been granted bail by a UAE court on the condition that he remains within the country, according to Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.

The Home Minister stated that while bail was granted, the full terms of the order are not yet known. He has requested certified copies of the order to understand the specific conditions.

In response to the gelişme, the Bangladesh government has appointed a law firm in the UAE to pursue the cancellation of Benazir Ahmed's bail.

Benazir Ahmed was arrested in Dubai in June following an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of the Bangladesh government.

The process to repatriate the former IGP to Bangladesh for trial is ongoing as the government continues its legal battle in the UAE.
